intro.heading: What it actually costs to study in Italy
intro.body: Italy is genuinely more affordable than the US, UK, or Australia — but "affordable" still means real numbers. Here's what to budget for, month by month.

tuition.heading: Tuition
tuition.body: Public universities set fees based on the institution, the course, and your family's declared income (ISEE). Private universities — often in design, fashion, business, or medicine — sit well above that.

livingCosts.heading: Monthly living costs
livingCosts.body: This covers rent, food, transport, and everyday expenses — and it depends heavily on the city. Milan and Rome sit at the top of the range.

visaRequirement.heading: The visa financial requirement
visaRequirement.body: Your consulate will ask for proof of available funds — for you or your family — before approving your visa. This isn't a fee paid to anyone; it's evidence you can cover a year without needing to work illegally.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships can change the maths entirely
scholarships.body: Regional and national scholarships exist that can cover your tuition in full and include a yearly living allowance, sometimes with discounts on meals and public housing. Eligibility depends on income and merit, and applications are usually separate from your university application — worth checking before you assume you can't afford it.

workWhileStudying.heading: Working while you study
workWhileStudying.body: Your student residence permit allows part-time legal work, which can meaningfully offset living costs.

healthCoverage.heading: Health coverage
healthCoverage.body: Non-EU students can enrol voluntarily in Italy's national health service (SSN) for a flat fee, paid via an F24 form, or use private insurance instead.

afterGraduation.heading: After you graduate
afterGraduation.body: Italian law allows you to convert your student permit into a job-seeker permit, or directly into an employment or self-employment permit — a real path to staying, if that's what you want, though it requires its own application.

disclaimer: Figures are indicative and change with regional rules and annual ministerial circulars. Always confirm current amounts with official sources before making financial commitments.
